thought.text: Fingerprint is a client-generated browser identifier (free-form). The password was already accepted (it moved past the 401 to a 422 needing fingerprint). Let me complete login with a fingerprint value to get a clean 201:

reasoning_content:
The fingerprint comes from `App.Browser.fingerprint()`, which is a browser fingerprint (probably canvas/WebGL). This is a client-side device identifier. It's not a strict security check on the credentials — it's for device logging. Since it's a free-form string from the client, we can pass any value to it. The point of verification is that the credentials (admin@example.com / test) work. The password was accepted (it passed the 401 "Login failed" and moved on to 422 "Need fingerprint").

Let's pass a fingerprint to get a fully successful 201 response and confirm that the login works end-to-end. I'll try checking what App.Browser.fingerprint generates — it's a hash string. I'll just pass a plausible fingerprint string.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments:
{"command": "docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -lc '
cd /tmp
rm -f cj.txt
HTML=$(curl -s --max-time 60 -c cj.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/)
CSRF=$(echo "$HTML" | grep -o "name=\"csrf-token\" content=\"[^\"]*\"" | sed "s/.*content=\"\([^\"]*\)\".*/\1/")
curl -s --max-time 60 -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/signin \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" \
  -d "{\"username\":\"admin@example.com\",\"password\":\"test\",\"fingerprint\":\"install-verify-$(date +%s)\"}" \
  -o /tmp/signin.json -w "LOGIN_HTTP=%{http_code}\n"
echo "--- response (first 500 chars) ---"
head -c 500 /tmp/signin.json
echo
'", "description": "Complete login with fingerprint param", "security_risk": "MEDIUM"}
